project.name: Minimal primes over principal ideals in semirings with unique factorization
project.description: Classifies minimal primes over nonzero principal ideals in commutative semirings with unique factorization by normalized irreducible factor values. Relates these factors to order-dual irreducible components of principal zero loci. For principal quotients in commutative rings with unique factorization, identifies associated primes with minimal primes over the principal ideal for every generator, and characterizes quotient-spectrum points by associated primes and exact annihilators. For arbitrary dependent families of semifields, classifies all prime ideals of the product by ultrafilters, with zero-set membership, evaluation and germ-kernel bridges, and finite-coordinate and infinite non-coordinate controls. The same equivalence is a homeomorphism for the Zariski and existing Stone topologies, with both basis pullback laws and dense coordinate primes. For arbitrary filters and independently universed dependent monoids with zero, the total-section filter product is reduced exactly when its reduced fibres form a filter member. For dependent semiring fibres, equips the existing total-section Filter.Product with semiring operations, fibrewise maps and principal-filter restriction equivalences. Ultrafilters give division semirings and semifields with pointwise inversion. The section-map kernels are the existing zero-set ideals, compatibly with constant-family germs. For arbitrary dependent type families, the total-section filter product is nontrivial exactly when a total section exists and nontrivial fibres occur frequently. Associated primes also transport along compatible algebra maps. In commutative rings with well-founded DvdNotUnit, prime generators give principal ideals of height at most one, with height one for non-zero-divisors and for prime elements in domains. Finite ambient initial height gives well-founded lower intervals in preorders and stabilization of antitone prime chains over commutative semirings, with an ideal interface over commutative rings using only initial FiniteHeight and primeness at every index. Both chain interfaces identify the all-index ideal infimum at the same tail index. For integral homomorphisms of arbitrary commutative rings in independent universes, bounds target Krull dimension by source dimension, with equality for injective maps. Without injectivity, the target has the dimension of the source modulo the kernel. A faithful integral algebra has the dimension of its base ring for its given algebra structure. These results use the full WithBot ℕ∞ dimension, including zero rings and infinite dimension. Minimal primes over arbitrary ideals of finite dependent products of commutative semirings correspond to labelled coordinate minimal primes, using the evaluation-image coordinates of Ideal.piOrderIso. Evaluation comap transports minimality over arbitrary ideals without finiteness of the index. The finite classification includes empty indices, subsingleton factors and whole base ideals, and retains the labels of repeated isomorphic factors. For arbitrary finite sets and WithBot ℕ∞ values, the bottom-aware successor of the nonempty-subset product sum equals the product of successors in ℕ∞, including empty indices and arbitrary bottom and top values. For arbitrary dependent families of given preorders in independent universes, the height and coheight of a supplied section in the original pointwise order are the suprema of finite coordinate-rank sums in ENat. For finite indices these are the coordinate sums, including empty indices and infinite ranks. The dimension of an arbitrary dependent pointwise product is the supremum of its finite coordinate-restriction image dimensions, with inherited subtype orders. An empty full product makes every image empty, including at the empty coordinate set. Over a finite linearly ordered index, their canonical lexicographic point ranks are sums of original coordinate ranks weighted by the whole later fibres' strict-chain vertex heights, with the same suffix priority for height and coheight. For any relation and finite family of disjoint cross-comparable sets, chain height is the sum of piece heights, with both hypotheses restricted to the chosen support.

sources.title: The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry

highlights.title: Prime spectra of products of semifields
highlights.statement: The prime spectrum of an arbitrary dependent product of semifields is canonically homeomorphic to the Stone space of ultrafilters on its index type.

highlights.title: Ideals in products of division semirings
highlights.statement: Every left ideal of an arbitrary dependent product of division semirings is the zero-set ideal of its characteristic-test filter.

highlights.title: Nontrivial dependent reduced products
highlights.statement: For every filter and independently universed dependent type family, the total-section reduced product is nontrivial exactly when a total section exists and nontrivial fibres occur frequently.

highlights.title: Krull dimension and chain cardinalities of lexicographic sums
highlights.statement: For arbitrary subsets of independently universed dependent preorders whose active indices form a finite strict chain, the stock lexicographic Sigma dimension is the active-index dimension plus the sum of active fiber dimensions. Empty support and infinite fiber dimensions are included. For two arbitrary preorder subsets, the tagged lexicographic union has the maximum of their dimensions and their sum plus one. For arbitrary subsets of independently universed dependent sums with raw relations, chain height is the supremum of finite sums of fiber heights, assuming only pairwise comparability and irreflexivity of the active indices. Empty fibers and infinite heights are allowed, with no transitivity, global order, finiteness or attainment hypothesis.

highlights.title: Dimension and point ranks of finite dependent lexicographic products
highlights.statement: For arbitrary subsets of independently universed given preorders over a finite linearly ordered index, lexicographic dimension is the WithBot map of ENat decrement applied to the product of the shifted fibre dimensions. Product and addition are in WithBot ENat, with only the decrement in ENat. Empty index, empty fibres and infinite dimensions are included. The canonical partial order is equality or strict lexicographic comparison with equality prefixes; it needs only strict less-than relations on the fibres and agrees as a whole record with Mathlib's construction when the fibres have partial orders. For a given section of arbitrary given fibre preorders, height and coheight are sums of the original coordinate ranks weighted by the strict-chain vertex heights of whole later fibres. Both use the same original suffix priority. These ENat formulas include empty indices and unattained infinite heights, with no fibre partial-order, linearity, finiteness or extra inhabitation premise.

headlines.title: Successors of finite product expansions
headlines.text:
For arbitrary `ι : Type u`, `J : Finset ι` and `d : ι → WithBot ℕ∞`,
[`ENat.WithBot.succ_sum_powerset_nonempty`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Data/ENat/BigOperators.lean)
states that the bottom-aware successor of the sum of `∏ i ∈ U, d i` over nonempty
subsets `U` of `J` equals `∏ i ∈ J, WithBot.succ (d i)`. The equality is in `ℕ∞`;
the subset products and their sum are in `WithBot ℕ∞`. Empty `J` and arbitrary
bottom and top values are included, with no decidable-equality premise on `ι`.
The proof reuses Mathlib's whole finite-product expansion `Finset.prod_add_one`.

headlines.title: Ranks of dependent pointwise products
headlines.text:
For arbitrary `ι : Type u`, independently universed given preorders
`β : ι → Type v`, and a section `f : ∀ i, β i`,
[`Order.height_pi_eq_iSup_finset` and `Order.coheight_pi_eq_iSup_finset`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
state

```lean
Order.height f = ⨆ s : Finset ι, ∑ i ∈ s, Order.height (f i)
Order.coheight f = ⨆ s : Finset ι, ∑ i ∈ s, Order.coheight (f i)
```

The supremum includes every finite coordinate set, including the empty set.
No finite-support condition on `f` or finiteness assumption on the index is needed.
Infinitely many positive finite coordinate ranks, or one infinite coordinate rank,
can give infinite rank. The proof detects each finite strict series on finitely
many coordinates and reuses the finite product formula on that restriction;
the reverse bound fills the remaining coordinates with the supplied `f`.

For a finite index `ι : Type u`, independently universed given preorders
`β : ι → Type v`, and a section `f : ∀ i, β i`,
[`Order.height_pi` and `Order.coheight_pi`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
state

```lean
Order.height f = ∑ i, Order.height (f i)
Order.coheight f = ∑ i, Order.coheight (f i)
```

These are equalities in `ℕ∞` for the original pointwise product preorder and the
original fibre preorders, including infinite ranks and unbounded finite chain
lengths with no attaining chain. No antisymmetry, fibre inhabitation, finite-height
or attainment hypothesis is required. An empty index gives both ranks zero;
the top of the pointwise `Fin 2 → Fin 2` square has height two, not lexicographic
rank three. The proofs compose the binary rank identities with Mathlib's
order-isomorphism rank invariance, canonical finite-Pi head/tail splitting and
reindexing, and finite-sum formulas.

headlines.title: Dimension from finite coordinate-restriction images
headlines.text:
For arbitrary `ι : Type u` and independently universed given preorders
`β : ι → Type v`,
[`Order.krullDim_pi_eq_iSup_range_restrict`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
states

```lean
Order.krullDim (∀ i, β i) =
  ⨆ J : Finset ι,
    Order.krullDim (Set.range
      (fun f : (∀ i, β i) => fun j : J => f j.1))
```

The equality is in `WithBot ℕ∞`. Every range has the inherited ordinary pointwise
subtype order, and every restriction starts from the original full product.
Thus an empty full product makes every image empty, even for `J = ∅`, giving
bottom on both sides. An empty ambient index instead gives dimension zero.
No nonemptiness, finite-index, finite-fibre, antisymmetry, finite-rank,
attainment or finite-support hypothesis is required; an infinite supremum need
not be attained by a finite image. These are not lexicographic or topological
products. The proof combines the point-height formulas above with Mathlib's
height transport, finite updates and surjective range reindexing.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of unions
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary relation `r` and subsets `s`, `t` of any type,
[`Set.chainHeight_union_le`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) gives
`(s ∪ t).chainHeight r ≤ s.chainHeight r + t.chainHeight r`.
The pieces may overlap or be empty; neither relation laws nor finite heights or
attainment are required. The proof restricts each comparable subset to its two
intersections and uses `ENat` cardinality subadditivity.

For disjoint pieces with `∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ t, r a b ∨ r b a`,
[`Set.chainHeight_union_of_disjoint_of_cross`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
gives equality: `(s ∪ t).chainHeight r = s.chainHeight r + t.chainHeight r`.
Cross comparisons need not have a consistent direction. The binary lexicographic-sum
formula below reuses this common-ambient union result.

For an arbitrary relation `q : X → X → Prop`, family `P : κ → Set X` and
`J : Finset κ`, the finite-family formula
[`Set.chainHeight_biUnion_finset_of_disjoint_of_cross`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
states
`(⋃ i ∈ J, P i).chainHeight q = ∑ i ∈ J, (P i).chainHeight q`.
Pairwise disjointness and cross comparability are required **only on `J`**:
for distinct `i,j ∈ J`, the pieces are disjoint and every point of `P i` compares
with every point of `P j` in either direction. There are no relation laws,
ambient finiteness, decidable-equality, nonemptiness or attainment assumptions.
Empty pieces and unbounded, unattained chain heights are included.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of exclusive-piece unions
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary relation `r` on `α : Type u` and a family `s : ι → Set α` with
independent `ι : Sort v`,
[`Set.chainHeight_iUnion_of_not_rel`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) gives
`(⋃ i, s i).chainHeight r = ⨆ i, (s i).chainHeight r` when points in
`s i \ s j` and `s j \ s i` cannot compare for every ordered pair `i,j`.
For each pair, the no-cross condition concerns only its opposite exclusive pieces;
all loops remain unrestricted. The family need not be directed, finite or nonempty,
and no relation laws or attainment are assumed.
The heights are `ENat` vertex cardinalities: the empty union and empty supremum are
zero, a singleton has height one, and unbounded finite chain sizes give top.

The proof shows that the traces of each chain on the pieces are inclusion-directed
and applies the existing directed-union formula to those traces. It does not choose
one piece containing the whole chain: nested finite initial segments of an infinite
chain satisfy the hypothesis but no piece contains their union.
The retained `Set.chainHeight_union_of_not_rel` is the Bool-family corollary, giving
the two-piece maximum formula with the same exclusive-piece hypothesis.

headlines.title: Krull dimension of exclusive-piece unions
headlines.text:
For a given preorder on `α : Type u`, an arbitrary independent `ι : Sort v`, and
`s : ι → Set α`,
[`Order.krullDim_iUnion_of_not_lt`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean) states
`Order.krullDim (⋃ i, s i) = ⨆ i, Order.krullDim (s i)` when points in
`s i \ s j` and `s j \ s i` satisfy `¬ a < b` for every ordered pair `i,j`.
All membership subtypes inherit the given preorder. No antisymmetry, inhabitation,
finiteness, directedness or attainment is assumed.

The finite-cut comparisons `Order.le_krullDim_iff_le_chainHeight` and
`Order.krullDim_le_iff_chainHeight_le` relate dimension bounds `n : ℕ` to
strict-chain height bounds `n + 1`, without assuming finite height. Dimension lies
in `WithBot ℕ∞` and counts strict steps, whereas chain height lies in `ℕ∞` and
counts vertices. Empty sets have values bottom and zero, singletons zero and one,
and unbounded finite chains give top. These generic order interfaces are
Mathlib-upstream candidates.

headlines.title: Dimension comparison and arbitrary unions
headlines.text:
For arbitrary subsets of independently universed given preorders,
[`Order.krullDim_le_krullDim_iff_chainHeight_le_chainHeight`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
states
`κ(s) ≤ κ(t) ↔ H(s) ≤ H(t)`, where `κ` is the dimension of the membership
subtype in `WithBot ℕ∞` and `H` is ambient strict-chain vertex height in `ℕ∞`.
There is no map between the carriers, and each subtype inherits its given preorder.
Empty sets have values bottom and zero; singletons have values zero and one.
Distinct equivalent preorder points do not form a strict step. Infinite values
include unbounded finite chains without a longest or infinite chain.

For arbitrary subsets in one given preorder, `Order.krullDim_union_le` states
`κ(s ∪ t) ≤ κ(s) ⊔ κ(t) ⊔ (κ(s) + κ(t) + 1)`.
No disjointness, upper/lower closure, directedness, antisymmetry, nonemptiness,
finiteness or attainment is assumed. All right-hand operations are in `WithBot ℕ∞`;
the separate joins preserve the other dimension when one piece is empty, even at top.
In the five-point total order, the alternating pieces `{0, 2, 4}` and `{1, 3}`
have dimensions two and one, while their union has dimension four: the additive
term is sharp and a maximum-only bound fails. Overlap is also allowed.

The comparison extends the finite-cut dimension/height equivalences to arbitrary
bounds, including bottom and top. The arbitrary-union bound relates the existing
`Set.chainHeight_union_le` and `Set.chainHeight_toLex_sum` height formulas to the
exact dimension formula `Order.krullDim_toLex_sum` for lexicographic sums.
These interfaces build on Mathlib's subtype orders, Krull dimension, strict-chain
height and extended-natural arithmetic.

headlines.title: Krull dimension under finite covers
headlines.text:
For one given preorder on `α : Type u`, an independent index `ι : Type v`,
`I : Finset ι`, a family `s : ι → Set α`, and `t ⊆ ⋃ i ∈ I, s i`,
[`Order.krullDim_le_iSup_of_subset_biUnion_finset`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
states

```lean
Order.krullDim t ≤
  ⨆ J ∈ I.powerset, ⨆ (_ : J.Nonempty),
    (∑ i ∈ J, Order.krullDim (s i)) + ((J.card - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
```

All membership subtypes inherit the given preorder. The pieces may overlap or be
empty; there is no finiteness, antisymmetry, closure or attainment assumption on the
ambient order. Subtraction takes place in the natural numbers before casting.
Restricting to nonempty subfamilies makes the bound bottom for an empty family or
an all-empty cover, while singleton subfamilies preserve a piece of top dimension.
The three singleton pieces of a three-point total order give the sharp term two
from the full subfamily. A literal finite union is the reflexive-inclusion application.
The finite chain-height sum bound is already supplied by Mathlib's
`Finset.apply_union_le_sum` applied to `Set.chainHeight_empty` and
`Set.chainHeight_union_le`, followed by `Set.chainHeight_mono` for subsets.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of disjoint sums
headlines.text:
For arbitrary relations `rα`, `rβ` on independently universed types and arbitrary
sets `s`, `t`, [`Set.chainHeight_sum_liftRel`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
gives chain height `max (s.chainHeight rα) (t.chainHeight rβ)` for the union of the
two tagged images under `Sum.LiftRel rα rβ`. No cross-tag points compare.
[`Set.chainHeight_sum`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) gives the same formula
for ordinary `α ⊕ β` less-than, induced by precisely the two given `LT` records.
Neither result requires relation laws, nonemptiness, finiteness or attainment.

The heights are `ENat` vertex cardinalities: two nonempty antichains have disjoint-sum
height one, unlike lexicographic-sum height two. Empty factors contribute zero;
unbounded finite heights are included without assuming an infinite or longest chain.
The proof specializes the exclusive-piece maximum formula above, reusing Mathlib's
relation embeddings and image-height transport to identify the two tagged-piece heights.

headlines.title: Finite localization near a minimal prime
headlines.text:
For a finite-type algebra over any commutative ring, module finiteness of the
residue-field fibre at a minimal prime gives finiteness after inverting an element
outside that prime. The map is the canonical localization of the given algebra map.
[`Algebra.FiniteType.exists_finite_awayMap_of_mem_minimalPrimes`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrimeLocalization.lean)
requires no reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis and includes the zero algebra.
The supporting [nil-integrality lemmas](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/IntegralNilpotent.lean)
lift monic relations using individual nilpotence rather than a uniformly nilpotent ideal.

headlines.title: Directed suprema of relations on a fixed set
headlines.text:
For any type `α` and fixed subset `s`,
[`Set.scottContinuous_chainHeight`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) states that
`r ↦ s.chainHeight r` is Scott continuous for the pointwise implication order on relations
`α → α → Prop`. No order or relation laws on `α` are needed. Scott continuity preserves
suprema of **nonempty directed** families, not arbitrary joins or bottom.

For a directed family `r : ι → α → α → Prop`, with independent `ι : Sort v`,
[`Set.chainHeight_iSup_of_directed`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) gives
`H(⨆ i, r i) = H(⊥) ⊔ ⨆ i, H(r i)`, where `H(r) = s.chainHeight r` takes values in
`ENat` and `⊔` is maximum. The false-relation baseline is zero for empty `s` and one
otherwise; it is essential when `ι` is empty. The proof captures all distinct-point
comparisons of a finite chain in one relation, without sorting or assuming attainment.

headlines.title: Directed unions: chain cardinality and order dimension
headlines.text:
For an inclusion-directed family `s : ι → Set α`, with independent carrier and
index universes and an arbitrary index `ι : Sort v`,
[`Set.chainHeight_iUnion_of_directed`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
identifies the `ENat` chain height of the union with the supremum of the piece
heights for **any relation** on `α`. With only a preorder on `α`,
[`Order.krullDim_iUnion_of_directed`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
gives the analogous equality for the induced subtype orders in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
The relation invariant counts vertices; order dimension counts strict steps.
Empty unions have values zero and bottom respectively, and infinite suprema
need not be attained by a piece. No nonemptiness, antisymmetry or finite-height
assumption is required. The proofs capture finite chain witnesses in one piece;
they do not select a longest or infinite chain. These are relation-height and
induced-order formulas, not topological subspace dimension formulas.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of lexicographic products
headlines.text:
For arbitrary relations `rα`, `rβ` on independently universed types and arbitrary
sets `s`, `t`, [`Set.chainHeight_prod_lex`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
proves that the chain height of `s ×ˢ t` for `Prod.Lex rα rβ` is the product of
the factor chain heights, provided `rα` is irreflexive **on `s`**. Neither relation
needs to be transitive; the second may have loops. `Set.chainHeight_toLex_prod`
transports this formula to the canonical less-than relation on the image under `toLex`,
with only `LT` on both types and first-relation `Std.Irrefl`.

These are `ENat` **vertex cardinalities**, not edge counts, Krull dimensions or
ordinal ranks. Empty factors give zero even beside infinite height. The proof
uses products of comparable subsets for the lower bound and finite first-coordinate
fibre counting for the upper bound, so it neither sorts a nontransitive comparable
set nor assumes a longest chain exists. It does not assert the analogous formula
for canonical weak `≤` in arbitrary preorders.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of lexicographic sums
headlines.text:
For arbitrary relations `rα`, `rβ` on independently universed types and arbitrary
sets `s`, `t`, [`Set.chainHeight_sum_lex`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean)
proves that the union of the two injection images has chain height
`s.chainHeight rα + t.chainHeight rβ` for `Sum.Lex rα rβ`. Within each tag the
factor relation is used, and every left-tagged point precedes every right-tagged
point. No irreflexivity, transitivity, nonemptiness or finiteness is assumed.
`Set.chainHeight_toLex_sum` transports the formula under `toLex` to the canonical
less-than relation on `α ⊕ₗ β`, using only the given `LT` records on both factors.

The heights count vertices in `ENat`: two singleton blocks, or two nonempty
antichains, give height two. The disjoint relation `Sum.LiftRel`, used by ordinary
Sum less-than, is different. Empty factors contribute zero, including beside top.
The proof applies the disjoint cross-comparable union formula and Mathlib's
relation-embedding transport. Its union core glues subset chains by cross comparison,
without sorting chains or assuming their heights are attained. Unbounded finite
chain cardinalities are included.

headlines.title: Chain cardinalities of dependent lexicographic sums
headlines.text:
For independent universes `ι : Type u` and `α : ι → Type v`, raw relations
`r : ι → ι → Prop` and `R : ∀ i, α i → α i → Prop`, and any
`S : Set (Σ i, α i)`,
[`Set.chainHeight_sigma_lex`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/ChainHeight.lean) proves

```lean
S.chainHeight (Sigma.Lex r R) =
  ⨆ J : Finset ι, ∑ i ∈ J, ((Sigma.mk i) ⁻¹' S).chainHeight (R i)
```

The assumptions are exactly `IsChain r (Sigma.fst '' S)` and
`∀ i ∈ Sigma.fst '' S, ¬ r i i`: distinct active indices compare in either
direction, and active indices have no loops. No transitivity, global index order,
finiteness, decidable equality, nonemptiness or countability is required. Directed
cycles and bidirectional comparisons on distinct indices are allowed. Inactive
indices may have loops, and empty fibers contribute zero. Dropping active
irreflexivity would let an index loop compare fiber points regardless of `R i`.

Heights count vertices in `ENat`. The empty finite support is available even for
an empty index type. The finite-support supremum can be top without a maximizing
support. Separately, a single fiber can have height top with no infinite chain.
The formula assumes neither form of attainment. The proof transports each active
fiber's height through `Sigma.mk`, applies the disjoint union formula by finite
induction, and uses the existing inclusion-directed union theorem for the union of
all finite partial unions.

headlines.title: Krull dimension of dependent lexicographic sums
headlines.text:
For independently universed given preorders `ι : Type u` and `α : ι → Type v`,
[`Order.krullDim_toLex_sigma`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean) applies to any
`S : Set (Σ i, α i)` whose active image `I = Sigma.fst '' S` is finite and a
strict chain for the given index preorder. It states

```lean
Order.krullDim (toLex '' S) = Order.krullDim I +
  ∑ i ∈ hI.toFinset, Order.krullDim ((Sigma.mk i) ⁻¹' S)
```

Here `hI : I.Finite`; `I` is only prose notation for the ordinary image.
The left subtype inherits the stock Sigma lexicographic preorder, and all index
and fiber subtypes inherit their given preorders. The ambient index can be infinite;
no antisymmetry, global fiber inhabitation, finite dimension or attainment is assumed.
The family form follows by taking `S = Set.univ.sigma s`.

The equation lies in `WithBot ℕ∞`. Empty support gives bottom plus an empty sum.
Inactive empty fibers are excluded: support `{0, 2}` in ℕ with singleton fibers
has dimension one, not the dimension of the ambient interval. A singleton active
support gives exactly its fiber dimension, including top. Distinct equivalent
preorder points supply no strict step, and top needs no longest or infinite chain.
The proof consumes the whole dependent-sum height formula above, collapses its
finite-partial-sum supremum, and uses the original dimension/height finite cuts
and stock successor and finite-sum arithmetic, not another chain construction.
`Order.succ_krullDim_eq_chainHeight` records the bottom-aware normalization:
`WithBot.succ (Order.krullDim s) = s.chainHeight (· < ·)`.

headlines.title: Krull dimension of lexicographic sums
headlines.text:
For arbitrary subsets `s`, `t` of independently universed preorders,
[`Order.krullDim_toLex_sum`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean) gives
`κ(L) = κ(s) ⊔ κ(t) ⊔ (κ(s) + κ(t) + 1)` in `WithBot ℕ∞`, where
`L = toLex '' (Sum.inl '' s ∪ Sum.inr '' t)` and each dimension uses the
membership subtype with its inherited preorder. No antisymmetry, nonemptiness,
finite height or attainment is assumed. This generic order formula is a
Mathlib-upstream candidate.

The separate terms retain the other dimension when a factor is empty: bottom
absorbs addition even beside top. Heights two and three give dimension four;
two nonempty antichains give lexicographic dimension one, unlike ordinary Sum's
zero. Infinite dimension includes unbounded finite chain lengths without a
longest or infinite chain. The proof uses the whole lexicographic height formula
and the finite-cut comparisons above, rather than another chain construction.

headlines.title: Krull dimension of lexicographic products
headlines.text:
For arbitrary subsets `s`, `t` of independently universed preorders,
[`Order.krullDim_toLex_prod`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean) states
`κ(toLex '' (s ×ˢ t)) = κ(s) * κ(t) + κ(s) + κ(t)` in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
The carrier is the membership subtype of that image in `α ×ₗ β`, with the
`Prod.Lex` preorder of the given factor preorders. Ties in the first coordinate
require equality, not preorder equivalence. No antisymmetry, nonemptiness,
finiteness or attainment is assumed.

An empty factor gives bottom even beside top. In the stock arithmetic,
`⊥ * 0 = 0`, but the explicit bottom summand still absorbs the whole polynomial.
A singleton factor preserves the other dimension, including bottom and top;
top with dimension zero gives top despite its zero multiplication term.
Two distinct equivalent first coordinates with three-point chain fibres give
two incomparable fibres and dimension two. Infinite dimension includes
unbounded finite chains without a longest or infinite chain.
`Fin 2 ×ₗ Fin 3` has dimension five, whereas its pointwise product has dimension
three and its tagged lexicographic sum has dimension four.
The vertex-height input is the existing whole `Set.chainHeight_toLex_prod`
formula, together with the finite-cut dimension comparisons above.

headlines.title: Point heights and coheights of binary lexicographic products
headlines.text:
For independently universed given preorders `α : Type u`, `β : Type v` and points
`a : α`, `b : β`, put `Hβ = (Set.univ : Set β).chainHeight (· < ·)`. The formulas
[`Order.height_toLex_prod` and `Order.coheight_toLex_prod`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
are

```text
height (toLex (a, b))   = height a   * Hβ + height b
coheight (toLex (a, b)) = coheight a * Hβ + coheight b
```

All arithmetic is in `ℕ∞`. Both use the same whole-second-factor strict-chain
**vertex cardinality**, not its Krull dimension, the rank of `b`, or the cardinality
of `β`. The target retains Mathlib's binary `Prod.Lex` preorder on `α ×ₗ β`:
`toLex (a, b) ≤ toLex (a', b')` means `a < a'` or `a = a' ∧ b ≤ b'`;
strict comparison replaces the second `≤` by `<`. Distinct weakly equivalent
first coordinates therefore give incomparable fibres. Within a fixed first
coordinate, distinct weakly equivalent second points remain mutually weakly
comparable. This is the binary preorder, not the equality-or-strict partial order
on dependent functions or the pointwise product order.

The supporting identities `Order.height_eq_chainHeight_Iio` and
`Order.coheight_eq_chainHeight_Ioi` identify point height and coheight with the
strict-chain vertex heights of the original strict lower and upper segments.
They use the given preorder's strict relation, without decomposing a closed
segment into its strict segment and an endpoint, which fails for general preorders.
There is no linearity, antisymmetry, finiteness, decidable equality, global
nonemptiness, bottom/top, finite-height or attainment hypothesis. The supplied
points inhabit both factors; empty strict segments have height zero, and
`0 * ⊤ = 0`. Infinite values include unbounded finite chains without a longest
or infinite chain.

The [middle-point client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/KrullDimension.lean) gives both
height four and coheight four at `toLex ((1 : Fin 3), (1 : Fin 3))`, whereas the
pointwise pair has both ranks two. Here `Hβ = 3`, not the second-factor dimension
two. The proofs combine the strict-segment identities with the existing whole
lexicographic product, disjoint-union, singleton-slice and direction-reversal
chain-height APIs.

headlines.title: Dimension and point ranks of finite dependent lexicographic products
headlines.text:
For a finite linearly ordered index `ι : Type u`, independently universed given
preorders `β : ι → Type v`, and subsets `s i`,
[`Order.krullDim_toLex_pi`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean) states

```lean
Order.krullDim (toLex '' Set.pi Set.univ s) =
  WithBot.map (fun h : ℕ∞ => h - 1)
    (∏ i, (Order.krullDim (s i) + 1 : WithBot ℕ∞))
```

The original dependent functions, their `toLex` image and all inherited membership
orders are retained. Product and addition take place in `WithBot ℕ∞`; only the
mapped decrement is in `ℕ∞`. An empty index gives dimension zero. An empty factor
gives bottom even beside top: although `0 * ⊥ = 0`, every shifted factor is nonzero.
A singleton index preserves dimension, including bottom and top. No fibre finiteness,
nonemptiness, antisymmetry, finite dimension or attainment is assumed.
The whole `Set.chainHeight_toLex_pi` formula supplies the product of vertex heights;
`Order.succ_krullDim_eq_chainHeight` relates those heights to the given dimensions.

The canonical order is supplied by
[`Pi.Lex.partialOrderOfLT`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/PiLex.lean). More generally, it needs
only a linearly ordered index and given fibre less-than relations with `IsStrictOrder`.
It uses Mathlib's `partialOrderOfSO`, retaining the stock strict lexicographic relation;
its weak comparison is equality or strict comparison. The stored-LT and stored-LE
lemmas expose both relations, and `Pi.Lex.partialOrderOfLT_eq` identifies the whole
record with Mathlib's construction under the original fibre PartialOrder hypotheses.
Prefixes use equality, not preorder equivalence: distinct equivalent fibre elements
need not retain their weak comparisons, even at a singleton index. Thus dimension
agreement does not assert an order isomorphism with a nonantisymmetric fibre.

For the original index with `[Fintype ι] [LinearOrder ι]`, arbitrary given fibre
preorders `β : ι → Type v` independent of the index universe, and a given section
`f : ∀ i, β i`, the point-rank formulas
[`Order.height_toLex_pi` and `Order.coheight_toLex_pi`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)
are

```text
height (toLex f)   = ∑ i, height (f i)   * ∏ j > i, H j
coheight (toLex f) = ∑ i, coheight (f i) * ∏ j > i, H j
H j = (Set.univ : Set (β j)).chainHeight (· < ·)
```

All arithmetic is in `ℕ∞`. The target is exactly the existing canonical
`Pi.Lex.partialOrderOfLT` described above: equality or strict lexicographic
comparison, with equality prefixes, not the pointwise order or the binary
`Prod.Lex` weak fallback at the last coordinate. Every coordinate rank, strict
comparison and whole-fibre height uses the **original given fibre preorder**.
Both formulas use the **same suffix `j > i`**, with the original index priority.
The weights count strict-chain vertices in whole later fibres, not their
Krull dimensions, carrier cardinalities or the ranks of `f j`.

No fibre partial order, linearity or finiteness, global fibre inhabitation,
nonempty index, finite height, attainment, decidable equality, bounds, coherence
or separate irreflexivity premise is required. Empty strict cuts give zero,
including beside infinite suffix weights since `0 * ∞ = 0`; an empty index gives
both ranks zero. Infinite heights may be unbounded without an attaining chain.
A singleton index preserves point ranks, not necessarily the fibre's weak order.

The [middle-section client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/PiLexRanks.lean) uses `Fin 3`
for both index and every fibre, with `f i = 1`. Both lexicographic ranks are
`1 * 9 + 1 * 3 + 1 * 1 = 13`, while the original pointwise ranks are
`1 + 1 + 1 = 3`. To distinguish priority, with first fibre `Fin 2`, second fibre
`Fin 3` and point `(1,1)`, coheight is `0 * 3 + 1 = 1`, not the value
`1 * 2 + 0 = 2` obtained by reversing priority.

The proofs decompose the original strict lower and upper cones into first-change
rectangles and compose the existing whole `Set.chainHeight_toLex_pi`, finite
disjoint cross-comparable union addition and original strict-cone/point-rank
bridges. They require no additional chain or enumeration construction.

headlines.title: Semimodules, annihilators and faithful actions on dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
For independent families `R i`, `M i` of semirings and additive commutative monoids,
with given `Module (R i) (M i)` records and an arbitrary filter `F`,
[`Filter.Product.module`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Module.lean) supplies
pointwise semimodule data on the existing `F.Product M` over the existing scalar
semiring `F.Product R`. The data are named rather than globally registered:
the given fibre actions stay fixed even when scalar and vector carriers coincide.
Representative equations characterize zero, addition, natural scaling and scalar
action. A represented scalar acts on every opaque vector by `Filter.Product.map`.
The additive record agrees with the existing semiring parent; constant records
recover Mathlib's two-germ module after identifying both base records.
The [torsion-free criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Torsion.lean)
`Filter.Product.isTorsionFree_iff` identifies torsion-freeness of this semimodule
over `F.Product R` with eventual torsion-freeness of the given fibre semimodules.
Torsion-freeness uses full injectivity of the action of every two-sided regular
scalar. The represented-scalar readout reduces action injectivity to eventual
fibre injectivity, and regular-scalar sections give reflection. No additive
inverses, cancellation, domain, properness or nontriviality assumption is required.
The [varying-family client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/Module.lean)
applies the criterion to free semimodules of ranks `n + 1` over `ℕ × ZMod (n + 2)`
along the cofinite filter, and uses the faithfulness criterion for the same family.

The [annihilator and faithfulness criteria](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Faithful.lean)
retain these same given records. `Filter.Product.coe_mem_annihilator_iff` says that
a represented scalar annihilates the whole semimodule exactly when its values
annihilate the fibre semimodules eventually. `Filter.Product.faithfulSMul_iff`
says that the action is faithful exactly when the given fibre actions are faithful
eventually. Faithfulness compares **two scalars on all vectors**, unlike
represented-scalar injectivity; a zero annihilator does not characterize it at this
semiring floor. The weaker `faithfulSMul_smul_iff` needs only given fibre actions
and scalar/vector zeros, while `smul_coe_eq_smul_coe_iff` detects equality of two
represented actions using only vector zeros. These zeros provide total sections,
not zero-preservation laws. Bottom filters, empty indices and zero fibres remain
included, with independent scalar and vector universes.

headlines.title: Matrix rings over dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary filter `F`, given semirings `R i` and a fixed index type `J` with
`Fintype J` and `DecidableEq J`, the
[matrix leaf](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Matrix.lean) constructs
`Filter.Product.matrixRingEquiv` between `F.Product (fun i => Matrix J J (R i))`
and `Matrix J J (F.Product R)`. Its underlying equivalence composes the existing
finite-Pi equivalences. The source and target retain the given semirings and stock
matrix records: multiplication is a finite row-column sum, not pointwise entry
multiplication. Representative and all-point entry equations in both directions
form its characteristic interface. `Filter.Product.isUnit_matrix_coe_iff` states
invertibility of a represented matrix exactly on the eventual unit locus of those
same fibre matrices; it does not assert that each entry is a scalar unit.
Index, coefficient and matrix-index universes are independent; empty matrices,
empty index types, bottom filters and zero semirings are included. There are no
commutativity, ring, field, properness or nontriviality hypotheses.

headlines.title: Common finite bases of dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
For the same given semiring and semimodule records, a family of given bases
`b i : Module.Basis J (R i) (M i)` with **one common finite index** `J` induces
[`Filter.Product.basis`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Basis.lean) of
`F.Product M` over the existing scalar semiring `F.Product R`. Its vector at `j`
is represented by `fun i => b i j`, and coefficients are the existing varying
maps of the fibre coefficients, on represented and opaque vectors alike.
For standard function bases on `J → R i`, the whole coordinate equivalence agrees
with `Filter.Product.piComparison`. All four carrier universes are independent;
empty `J`, bottom filters and zero semirings are included. No commutativity,
faithfulness, properness or nontriviality hypothesis is imposed. A family of
unbounded varying ranks is not an instance of this common finite-index construction.

headlines.title: Uniform finite generators of dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
The [finite-generation module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Finite.lean)
proves two finite-generation criteria.
For the same given semiring, additive and module records, an arbitrary filter `F`,
a naturally finite index type `J` and raw vectors `g : J → (∀ i, M i)`,
`Filter.Product.span_range_coe_eq_top_iff` gives

```text
Submodule.span (F.Product R) (Set.range (fun j => (g j : F.Product M))) = ⊤
  ↔ ∀ᶠ i in F, Submodule.span (R i) (Set.range (fun j => g j i)) = ⊤.
```

The target records are exactly `Product.instSemiring`, `Product.addCommMonoid`
and `Product.module` of the given fibres, even when `R = M`.
`Filter.Product.moduleFinite_iff` gives

```text
Module.Finite (F.Product R) (F.Product M)
  ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ i in F, ∃ v : Fin n → M i,
      Submodule.span (R i) (Set.range v) = ⊤.
```

One uniform `n` is essential; eventual pointwise finite generation alone does
not give this condition. No basis or freeness is assumed. All four carrier
universes are independent. Empty `J`, `n = 0`, empty index types, bottom filters
and zero semirings are included, with no properness or nontriviality hypothesis.
These criteria add no new functional data or global instances.

headlines.title: Uniform finite presentations of dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
The [finite-presentation module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/FinitePresentation.lean)
proves the uniform generators-and-relations criterion. For arbitrary `F`,
independently universed ring families `R i`, and given additive
commutative monoids `M i` with their given `R i`-module actions,
`Filter.Product.moduleFinitePresentation_iff` gives

```text
Module.FinitePresentation (F.Product R) (F.Product M)
  ↔ ∃ n m : ℕ, ∀ᶠ i in F,
      ∃ f : (Fin n → R i) →ₗ[R i] M i,
      ∃ g : (Fin m → R i) →ₗ[R i] (Fin n → R i),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ Function.Exact g f.
```

The left side uses exactly `Product.instSemiring` of the ring semiring parents,
`Product.addCommMonoid` of the given vector records, and `Product.module` of the
given actions. Each `f` retains the given target addition and action, even when
`R = M`; only coefficient function spaces use standard self-actions. Exactness
uses the given vector zero. The pair `(n,m)` precedes the eventual quantifier;
eventual individual finite presentation or a generator bound alone is weaker.
Padding generators may require additional relations, so exact fixed sizes must
not be confused with independently padding both sizes at unchanged bounds.

The rings may be noncommutative, and coefficients act on the left. No properness,
nontriviality, freeness, coherence or Noetherian assumption is imposed. Bottom
filters, empty index types, zero rings/modules and zero free sizes are included.
Represented coordinate negation gives additive inverses for the named scalar
semiring; the given module actions give vector inverses without a new group
hypothesis. This is the genuine ring-module presentation scope. Over general
semirings Mathlib's stock class concerns a finitely generated zero kernel, not a
presentation by a finitely generated congruence; no such semiring claim is made.

headlines.title: Exactness of dependent reduced-product maps
headlines.text:
For arbitrary functions `f i : X i → Y i` and `g i : Y i → Z i` in independent
universes, an arbitrary filter `F`, given `Zero (Z i)` records and
`Nonempty (∀ i, X i)`,
[`Filter.Product.map_exact_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Exact.lean)
characterizes `Function.Exact` of the two existing `Product.map` functions by
`∀ᶠ i in F, Function.Exact (f i) (g i)`. This is one eventual locus of **whole
fibre exactness**, not exactness at every index or separately eventual tests on
fixed values. The selected target zero is exactly `Product.zeroPoint F Z`, the
represented section of the given fibre zeros; no global zero instance is added.
Neither function needs to preserve zero or any algebraic operation.

A total source section is essential: an empty source fibre outside the filter's
support still prevents all total source sections. No independent middle-section
hypothesis is needed, since the first map sends a source section to one.
`Filter.Product.map_exact_iff_of_addZeroClass` instead uses the existing named
additive product zero, still for arbitrary functions and only target
`AddZeroClass` records. `Product.zeroPoint_eq_zero_add` supplies this alignment.
In particular, given linear maps between semimodules over given, possibly
noncommutative, fibre semirings can be used as functions while retaining all the
given additive and module records. The target zero is inherited from
`Product.addCommMonoid F P`, and fibre source zeros discharge the section
condition. No bundled product linear map, finite basis, properness,
nontriviality, additive inverses or further inhabitation hypothesis is needed.
Bottom filters, empty indices and zero semirings remain included.

For constant families, `Product.map_const_eq_germ_map` and
`Product.zeroPoint_eq_germ_zero` identify these functions and the target zero
with Mathlib's germ maps and zero.

headlines.title: Coordinate maps and zero-reflection of dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For any filter `D` and independently universed dependent type families `R` and `S`,
coordinate functions `φ i : R i → S i` induce the canonical
[`Filter.Product.map`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Map.lean)
from `D.Product R` to `D.Product S`. Its representative law uniquely characterizes
it, with identity and composition laws and agreement with the existing semiring
and constant-family germ maps. No algebra, points or proper-filter hypothesis is
needed for the coordinate map.

If the coordinate functions preserve selected total sections `a` and `b`
eventually, the induced map reflects the represented point `b` to `a` exactly
when the coordinate functions reflect these points eventually. For fibrewise
`ZeroHom`s this gives zero-reflection using only the **same selected fibre zeros**:
`Filter.Product.zeroPoint` is the class of that zero section, not a new Product
zero instance. No multiplication, addition or scalar zero is required.

`Filter.Product.map_surjective_iff` retains the exact global-section alternatives:
the total target section type is empty, or the total source section type is
nonempty and the coordinate maps are surjective eventually. An empty source fibre
ignored by the filter cannot be silently filled. The
[dependent controls](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/Map.lean) include varying
`Fin (n + 3) → Fin (n + 4)` maps that reflect zero but are neither injective nor
additive, and a frequent bad locus giving a genuine nonzero kernel class.

headlines.title: Reindexing dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For independently universed indices and fibres, a map `u : ι → κ` with
`Tendsto u F G` induces
[`Filter.Product.compTendsto`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/CompTendsto.lean)
from `G.Product R` to `F.Product (fun i => R (u i))`. It sends a section to its
precomposition, respects identity and composition, and agrees with the existing
`Filter.Germ.compTendsto` on constant families. No algebra, total-section existence
or proper-filter assumption is needed. The full criterion
`compTendsto_injective_iff` says that pullback is injective exactly when the original
total-section type is empty or
`Filter.map u F ⊓ principal {j | Nontrivial (R j)} =
G ⊓ principal {j | Nontrivial (R j)}`. Exact filter-image equality therefore suffices
(`compTendsto_injective_of_map_eq`), without injectivity of `u`, but is not necessary
for a fixed family. An index equivalence makes pullback surjective with only forward
convergence (`compTendsto_surjective_of_equiv`), but not necessarily injective.
Convergence in both directions gives `Filter.Product.compTendstoEquiv`, whose inverse
uses canonical dependent Pi reindexing. The
[dependent Bool client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/CompTendsto.lean)
contrasts a four-to-two noninjective pullback with a two-to-two injective pullback
for the same unequal filters, by making the ignored fibre a singleton. It also
exhibits an injective, non-surjective diagonal.

The underlying
[`Filter.forall_eventually_eq_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Basic.lean) works for
fibres in any independently universed `Sort`: two filters give the same eventual
equality on all pairs of total sections exactly when there is no total section or
their restrictions to `{i | ∃ x y : R i, x ≠ y}` agree. For Type-valued families,
[`Filter.productSetoid_eq_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product.lean) expresses
this using the existing section setoids and stock `Nontrivial` support. An empty
fibre ignored by a filter still prevents total sections; eventual inhabitation
cannot replace the empty-total-section alternative.

headlines.title: Small products of dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary filter `D` and `R : ι → κ → Type w`, with independent row,
coordinate and fibre universes, [`Filter.Product.piComparison`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Pi.lean)
maps the class of a matrix to its family of column classes. It is surjective for
arbitrary `κ`. If `[CardinalInterFilter D c]` and `HasCardinalLT κ c`, with `c` in
the row universe, `Filter.Product.piEquivOfHasCardinalLT` makes this same comparison
an equivalence. The bound is strict: the filter must be closed under intersections
of fewer than `c` sets. Countable completeness and countable coordinates give
`Filter.Product.piEquivOfCountable`; finite coordinates give the original
`Filter.Product.piEquiv` for **every** filter. Both new equivalences agree with the
finite one as equivalence data when the coordinates are finite.

The inverse transposes supplied global column representatives. Generic equivalence
identities and the forward readouts give the inverse laws; existing comparison
naturality gives both naturality squares, with an independent target universe.
No quotient unfolding, algebra, inhabited fibres, properness, common-universe
assumption or chosen finite enumeration is required. The
[examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/Pi.lean) include infinite even
principal rows with `Fin (i+j+2)` fibres and proper nonprincipal cocountable rows
on `Set ℕ`, as well as empty indices and bottom with empty global sections.
The cofinite-Nat Boolean diagonal remains a failure of injectivity: countable
coordinates alone do not suffice.

headlines.title: Centers of dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For any filter and an independently universed family with multiplication, a section
represents an element of the full intrinsic center exactly when it is central
eventually. With a two-sided identity in each fibre,
[`Filter.Product.centerEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Center.lean)
identifies the product of the fibre centers with the center of the product.
Neither associativity nor a proper filter is required. The representative API
selects a total center-valued section agreeing eventually, not canonically at
ignored indices. The [varying-family client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Germ/Center.lean)
uses retained fibres of sizes four and sixteen with nonassociative multiplication;
the existing constant-germ API and its client remain available.

headlines.title: Reduced filter germs
headlines.text:
For independent index and value universes, any filter `D`, and a value type `M`
with only zero and natural-number powers,
[`Filter.Germ.isReduced_iff_eventually`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Germ/Reduced.lean)
characterizes reducedness of `Germ D M` by eventual reducedness of `M`.
Equivalently, `D = ⊥` or `M` is reduced. No power laws or properness assumption
are needed. The same module characterizes nilpotence by one exponent whose
power is zero eventually, and supplies reducedness for germs of reduced values.

headlines.title: Nontrivial dependent reduced products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary filter `D` and an independently universed dependent type family `R`,
[`Filter.Product.nontrivial_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Nontrivial.lean)
characterizes nontriviality of the existing total-section product by
`Nonempty (∀ i, R i)` and frequent nontriviality of the fibres. No algebraic,
fibre-inhabitation or proper-filter hypothesis is required. The section condition is
essential: an empty fibre outside the filter's support still makes the product empty.
The same module gives nonemptiness and subsingleton criteria, and the constant-family
characterization for `Filter.Germ`. The
[varying-fibre clients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/FilterProductNontrivial.lean) contrast a
trivial default fibre with an empty off-support fibre.

headlines.title: Reduced ranges of iterated Frobenius
headlines.text:
For a commutative semiring of exponential characteristic `p`, the original image
of the `n`th Frobenius iterate is reduced exactly when every nilpotent element
has zero `p ^ n`th power. If the semiring is Noetherian and `p` is prime,
all sufficiently high iterates have reduced images. The
[reduced-image API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Frobenius/Reduced.lean) also gives the
corresponding original subring-range statement for a given commutative ring.
No field, perfectness, or reducedness of the ambient semiring is assumed.

headlines.title: No zero divisors in ultrafilter products
headlines.text:
For an ultrafilter `U` and an independently universed dependent family `R`,
[`Filter.Product.noZeroDivisors_iff_eventually`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/NoZeroDivisors.lean)
characterizes no zero divisors in the product by eventual no zero divisors in the
fibres. It requires only `Zero` and `Mul` on each fibre and uses the existing
`Con.hasMul` and `Con.zero` operations on the existing product carrier. No
associativity, unit, absorption by zero, addition, commutativity or nontriviality
hypothesis is needed. For monoids with zero,
`Filter.Product.noZeroDivisors_iff` uses the canonical product instances; the
operation-agreement lemmas identify the same zero and multiplication.
The [varying finite client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/NoZeroDivisors.lean)
has no zero divisors even though zero is not absorbing.

The [constant-family bridge](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Germ/NoZeroDivisors.lean)
compares the congruence zero and multiplication records with the existing germ
operations for every filter. At an ultrafilter, `Filter.Germ.noZeroDivisors_iff`
therefore characterizes no zero divisors in the germ by no zero divisors in the
value type, still with only `Zero` and `Mul`. The same nonabsorbing client exercises
this specialization. These generic criteria are Mathlib-upstream candidates.

Eventual fibrewise no zero divisors alone does not suffice for arbitrary filters:
at the proper top filter on a two-point index type, complementary nonzero sections
over a domain multiply to zero.

For arbitrary `F`, if each fibre has a **two-sided absorbing zero** (`MulZeroClass`),
`Filter.Product.noZeroDivisors_iff_eventually_and_trace` characterizes no zero divisors
for the same congruence operations by the conjunction of eventual fibrewise no zero
divisors and `D = ⊥ ∨ IsAtom D`, where
`D = F ⊓ principal {i | Nontrivial (R i)}`. Both absorption laws are material; no unit,
associativity, properness or all-fibre nontriviality is required. The trace, not `F`
itself, must be bottom or an atom, and even an atomic trace does not remove the
fibrewise condition. The canonical monoid-with-zero specialization is
`Filter.Product.noZeroDivisors_iff_eventually_and_trace_of_monoidWithZero`.
The [mixed-fibre client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/NoZeroDivisors.lean)
uses top on Bool with a natural-number fibre and a singleton fibre: its trace is
`pure false`, so the product has no zero divisors although top is not an ultrafilter.

headlines.title: Reduced dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary filter and an independently universed dependent family of
monoids with zero, the filter product is reduced exactly when its reduced
fibres form a member of the filter. The
[criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Reduced.lean) uses a uniform
square-zero test, not an exchange of a varying nilpotence exponent with
eventual equality. A representative is nilpotent exactly when one uniform
natural-number exponent makes its power zero eventually; the exponent may be
zero. No addition, commutativity, proper-filter or nontriviality hypothesis is
needed.

If the filter contains a finite set, nilpotence of a represented section is
also equivalent to eventual fibrewise nilpotence, by
[`Filter.Product.isNilpotent_coe_iff_of_finite_mem`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Reduced.lean).
The whole index type need not be finite. The same module gives finite-index
and finite-principal criteria; the latter tests exactly the values on the
generating set, including the empty set. These results reuse the
[finite-member exponent bound](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Nilpotent.lean).
For **monoid-with-zero coefficients**, the
[constant-germ specialization](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Germ/Reduced.lean)
uses the existing germ zero and power operations; the earlier germ results
still need only zero and natural-number powers. The
[dependent client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/Nilpotent.lean) gives
a nonzero nilpotent quotient element on an infinite index type with varying
nonadditive fibres.

headlines.title: Regular elements of dependent filter products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary filter `D` and an independently universed family `K` with only
fibrewise multiplication, a total section represents a left-regular, right-regular,
or regular element of `D.Product K` exactly when its values have that property
eventually. The [criteria](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Product/Regular.lean) require
neither associativity, an identity, nor a proper filter. The existing
[Germ criteria](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/Filter/Germ/Regular.lean) are their constant-family
specializations. The [varying finite example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/Order/Filter/Product/Regular.lean)
separates left and right regularity in noncommutative magmas with no identity.

headlines.title: Integral pullback of maximal spectra
headlines.text:
For an integral homomorphism `f : R →+* S` of commutative rings in independent
universes,
[`MaximalSpectrum.comapOfIsIntegral`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Spectrum/Maximal/Map.lean)
maps `MaximalSpectrum S` to `MaximalSpectrum R` by ideal contraction. Its image
is exactly the maximal ideals containing `RingHom.ker f`, and it is surjective
when `f` is injective. The API gives the underlying-ideal equation, agreement
with prime-spectrum pullback, identity and contravariant composition.

For the existing Zariski topologies, this function is
[continuous and closed](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Spectrum/Maximal/Topology.lean).
It sends the maximal-spectrum trace of `V(I)` to the trace of `V(I.comap f)`
for every ideal `I` of `S`. Zero rings are allowed; no chosen algebra structure,
domain, Jacobson, Noetherian or finite-type assumption is imposed. Integral
pullback need not be injective, even when the ring homomorphism is injective.

For surjective `f`, the same function is the embedding
`MaximalSpectrum.comapEmbeddingOfSurjective`, with all the same compatibility
laws. The
[product-projection client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/RingTheory/Spectrum/Maximal/Map.lean)
uses this embedding to transport infinitude of the maximal spectrum from a factor
to the product ring with `Infinite.of_injective`.

headlines.title: Other headline results

headlines.text:
The following interfaces are implemented in this library. See the [reader guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/docs/Guide.md)
and the linked module documentation for statements, examples, proof ideas and Mathlib dependencies.

headlines.title: All ideals of products and standard filters
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/PiFilter.lean)). For a dependent family
`K : ι → Type v` of division semirings, `Ideal.piOrderIsoFilter K` identifies
`Ideal (Π i, K i)` with the order dual of `Filter ι`; in particular it applies
to semifields. Its characteristic law is
`{i | f i = 0} ∈ I.piFilter K ↔ f ∈ I`. Both constructors already work for
semirings, but division is used to recover every ideal. The improper filter
gives the whole ideal, a principal filter gives functions vanishing on its
generating set, and the cofinite filter gives finite support. The API includes
germ kernels, singly generated ideals, and compatibility with Mathlib's finite
coordinate-ideal classification. Index and factor universes are independent;
empty products are included without a nontrivial-product assumption.
For arbitrary semiring fibres, coordinate ideals `I i` and a filter `D`,
`Filter.pi_sup_piIdeal_eq_top_iff` says that `Ideal.pi I ⊔ D.piIdeal R` is
the whole ideal exactly when `{i | I i = ⊤} ∈ D`. The properness criterion
`Filter.pi_sup_piIdeal_ne_top_iff` is nonmembership of this set, not membership
of its complement unless `D` is an ultrafilter. Zero fibres and improper
filters are allowed.
([examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/RingTheory/Ideal/PiFilter.lean)).

headlines.title: Ultrafilter coordinate-locus criteria
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/PrimePiUltrafilter.lean)). For dependent
semirings `R i` and left ideals `I i`, `Ultrafilter.isPrime_pi_sup_piIdeal_iff`
and `Ultrafilter.isMaximal_pi_sup_piIdeal_iff` characterize the sum
`Ideal.pi I ⊔ (U : Filter ι).piIdeal R` as prime or maximal exactly when the
respective coordinate locus belongs to `U`. The criteria need no commutativity,
nontrivial-factor or subtractivity assumption.

headlines.title: Prime ideals of arbitrary products of semifields
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/PrimePiUltrafilter.lean)). For any dependent
family `K : ι → Type v` of semifields, `PrimeSpectrum.piEquivUltrafilter K`
identifies every prime ideal of `Π i, K i` with an ultrafilter on `ι`.
A function belongs to the ideal for `U` exactly when `{i | f i = 0} ∈ U`.
Already for **division-semiring** fibres, `Ultrafilter.piIdeal_isMaximal` makes
every such ultrafilter zero-set ideal maximal, via the ideal/filter order isomorphism.
The index universe is independent of `v`, and no additive cancellation, ring,
finite-index or nonempty-index hypothesis is imposed. The forward ideal construction
works already for semiring factors, with evaluation-kernel and constant-family
germ-kernel bridges. Finite products have uniquely labelled coordinate kernels;
the cofinite ultrafilter gives non-coordinate primes on infinite index types.
The [topological extension](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/PiUltrafilter.lean)
`PrimeSpectrum.piHomeomorphUltrafilter K` retains this exact equivalence as a
homeomorphism for the Zariski and existing Stone topologies. Its basis pullback
laws use the nonzero locus and the function one on a subset and zero off it.
Coordinate primes are dense, even when non-coordinate primes occur; the topology
is not in general discrete. For an arbitrary index map `g : κ → ι` and fibrewise
semifield homomorphisms `φ j : K (g j) →+* L j`, spectral pullback along the stock
product homomorphism corresponds to `Ultrafilter.map g`. The API includes the
inverse square, index precomposition and same-index family-map specializations;
the index and fibre universes are independent, with no injectivity or finiteness assumption.

headlines.title: Residue fields of dependent products of fields
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/ResidueFieldPiUltrafilter.lean)). For a
dependent family `K : ι → Type v` of fields and `U : Ultrafilter ι`,
`Ultrafilter.residueFieldProductEquiv K U` canonically identifies
`(U.piIdeal K).ResidueField` with the existing `(U : Filter ι).Product K`.
This is a ring equivalence over the section ring `R = Π i, K i`: for **every
section** `r`, it sends `algebraMap R (U.piIdeal K).ResidueField r` to the
reduced-product class of `r`. The API includes the inverse equation, uniqueness
from this property and its equality-of-homomorphisms form. Fibrewise field
homomorphisms give a commuting square with `Ideal.ResidueField.map` and
`Filter.Product.mapRingHom`. Index and fibre universes are independent; no
common characteristic, finite-index or nonempty-index hypothesis, or global
field instance on the Product, is required. The
[examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/ResidueFieldPiUltrafilter.lean) check the principal
coordinate kernel and a dependent `ZMod 2`/`ZMod 3` family with distinct residue
characteristics and opposite-characteristic nonzero controls.

headlines.title: Minimal primes of finite products
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrimePi.lean)). For commutative
semirings `R i` and a finite index type, `Ideal.mem_minimalPrimes_pi_iff`
identifies minimal primes over any ideal of the product with unique labelled coordinate
minimal primes. `Ideal.minimalPrimesPiEquiv` gives the corresponding equivalence
with the dependent sum of the minimal primes over `Ideal.piOrderIso I i`.
Its inverse is evaluation comap, with forward/comap and evaluation-image laws.
The transport theorem `Ideal.comap_eval_mem_minimalPrimes_iff` works even for
infinite index types; it does not classify all primes of an infinite product.
No nonempty-index, nontrivial-factor, proper-base-ideal or ring assumptions
are needed. Equal factors retain distinct coordinate labels.

headlines.title: Minimal primes and radical membership detected by localization
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrimeLocalization.lean)).
In a commutative semiring `R`, an element belongs to `I.radical` exactly when its
canonical image belongs to the radical of the extension of `I` in
`Localization.AtPrime q` for every minimal prime `q` over `I`
(`Ideal.mem_radical_iff_forall_minimalPrimes_localization`). The unit ideal is included.
The [natural-number client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimesTest/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrimeLocalization.lean)
shows that `2` passes these tests for `(4)` despite not belonging to `(4)`, while `1` fails.
For commutative semirings `R`, `A` with `[Algebra R A]`, a prime ideal `q`
and `[IsLocalization.AtPrime A q]`, any ideal `I` also satisfies
`(I.map (algebraMap R A)).radical = q.map (algebraMap R A)` iff `q ∈ I.minimalPrimes`.
No separate `I ≤ q` is needed. Mathlib supplies the implication from minimality.

headlines.title: Multipliers outside a minimal prime
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrimeMultipliers.lean)).
For ideals `I`, `q` in a commutative semiring, `q ∈ I.minimalPrimes` and `x ∈ q`
imply `∃ s ∉ q, s * x ∈ I.radical`. Over the zero ideal, the product is nilpotent.

headlines.title: Ideal contraction and positive powers in the image
headlines.text:
([ideals](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Ideal/PositivePowerRange.lean),
[prime spectra](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/PositivePowerRange.lean)).
For a homomorphism from a semiring `R` to a commutative semiring `S`, suppose
every `x : S` has some positive power in `Set.range f`. Then
`I.comap f ≤ J.comap f ↔ I ≤ J` for arbitrary `I` and radical `J`.
For every target ideal `I`,
`Ideal.radical_map_comap_of_pos_pow_mem_range` also gives
`(Ideal.map f (Ideal.comap f I)).radical = I.radical`.
The map may have any type with `FunLike` and `RingHomClass` instances, in an
independent universe. No surjectivity, uniform exponent or radicality of `I`
is assumed. For commutative semirings on both sides and a bundled homomorphism,
`PrimeSpectrum.isEmbedding_comap_of_pos_pow_mem_range` proves that the existing
`PrimeSpectrum.comap f` is a topological embedding, with independent source and
target universes. Its image need not be closed or the whole spectrum.

headlines.title: Dimension under field extension
headlines.text:
For fields `K` and `L`, a given
`[Algebra K L]`, and a commutative `K`-algebra `A` with
`[Algebra.FiniteType K A]`, the
[field-extension leaf](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/KrullDimension/FieldExtension.lean)
proves `Algebra.ringKrullDim_tensorProduct_of_finiteType`:
`ringKrullDim (A ⊗[K] L) = ringKrullDim A`. All three types may lie in
independent universes. The extension need not be algebraic, and `A` need not
be a domain, reduced or nontrivial. Dimension takes values in `WithBot ℕ∞`;
the zero algebra has dimension `⊥`.

headlines.title: Dimension under integral maps
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Integral.lean)).
For integral maps `f : R →+* S` of commutative rings, target Krull dimension is
at most source dimension, with equality if `f` is injective. Without injectivity,
`ringKrullDim S = ringKrullDim (R ⧸ RingHom.ker f)`. A faithful integral algebra
has equal source and target dimensions using its given algebra structure.
Dimensions lie in `WithBot ℕ∞`, including zero rings and infinite dimension.

headlines.title: Closed-locus dimension bound for ideals containing a non-zero-divisor
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Basic.lean)). For a commutative
semiring `R`, `PrimeSpectrum.krullDim_zeroLocus_add_one_le_of_exists_mem_nonZeroDivisors`
states that `Order.krullDim (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set R)) + 1 ≤ ringKrullDim R`
whenever `∃ a ∈ J, a ∈ nonZeroDivisors R`. Addition is in `WithBot ℕ∞`, so empty loci
retain dimension bottom and infinite dimensions are included. The finite-bound API
`PrimeSpectrum.krullDimLE_zeroLocus_of_exists_mem_nonZeroDivisors` also gives dimension
at most `n` under `[Ring.KrullDimLE (n + 1) R]`. The canonical closed locus carries the
inherited spectrum order. No prime element, principal or prime ideal, domain, unique
factorization, ring, Noetherian, properness or nonempty-locus assumption is imposed.
Neither form asserts equality or exact dimension subtraction.
For commutative rings, Mathlib's quotient-spectrum order isomorphism identifies
the same locus with the spectrum of `R ⧸ J`; arbitrary semiring ideal quotients
are not asserted.

headlines.title: Dimension from irreducible generators of prime ideals
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Basic.lean)). In any commutative
semiring, if every nonzero nonmaximal prime ideal is generated by an irreducible
element, `Ring.krullDimLE_two_of_forall_exists_irreducible_span_eq` gives
`Ring.KrullDimLE 2 R`. No domain, unique factorization, ring or Noetherian
assumption is required, and irreducible elements need not be prime.

headlines.title: Height and dimension of pointwise products
headlines.text:
([module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/minimal-primes/blob/45952e34e2da84045925cdfa45f0514356a2a608/MinimalPrimes/Order/KrullDimension.lean)). In arbitrary preorders,
`Order.height_pi` and `Order.coheight_pi` express the ranks of a section of a
finite dependent product as sums of its coordinate ranks in `ℕ∞`, including
infinite ranks and rank zero for an empty index. For arbitrary dependent products,
`Order.height_pi_eq_iSup_finset` and `Order.coheight_pi_eq_iSup_finset` give the
supremum of finite coordinate-rank sums, with no finite-support hypothesis.
`Order.krullDim_pi_eq_iSup_range_restrict` expresses the dimension of an arbitrary
dependent product as the supremum of its finite restriction-image dimensions,
retaining empty images when the full product is empty.
The binary formulas are
`Order.height_prod` and `Order.coheight_prod`.
`Order.krullDim_prod` and `Order.krullDim_pi` give the dimension of binary
